title: Many Lines of Output
goal: In this lesson you will learn how several print() calls make several lines of output.
learn: Each print() usually makes one new line
Stack print() calls for a longer message
Order of print() matches order of output
idea: One print() shows one line. Want three lines? Use three print() calls. Python still runs top to bottom, so the first print() appears first in the output, then the next, then the next.
changeOneLine: In the editor above, change Room 12 to Room 8. Press Run. Only that middle line of output should change.

practice.text: Finish the school schedule so it prints three class names on three lines. Fill in the blanks.
practice.hint: You already have Math on the first line. Each empty print() needs a different subject name in quotes.
practice.starterTip: Fill the two blank print() lines, for example print("Science") and print("Art").
practice.gradingNote: Pass if there are three print() calls that each show a non-empty class name or subject.

practice.text: Make a four-line shopping list. Keep the title. Fill in the three blank item lines.
practice.hint: Keep print("Shopping list") as line one. The three blank print() lines each need one item in quotes.
practice.starterTip: Try print("Apples"), print("Milk"), and print("Bread") on the three blank lines.
practice.gradingNote: Pass if there are four print() calls with non-empty text (title plus three items).

quiz.question: How do you print three separate lines?

options.text: Use one print() with no quotes
Use three print() calls, one after another
Python only allows one print per program

quiz.correct: Stack print() calls. Each one makes another line.
quiz.wrong: Comments do not print. You need multiple print() calls.

quiz.question: If print("A") is above print("B"), what appears first?

options.text: Both on the same line as AB

quiz.correct: Top to bottom: A prints before B.
quiz.wrong: Output follows the same top-to-bottom order as the code.

quiz.question: What happens if you delete one print() from a four-line poster program?

options.text: You usually get three lines of output

quiz.correct: Fewer print() calls usually means fewer output lines.
quiz.wrong: Each print() you keep still runs; the deleted one is gone.
